rules.description: All highlights removed
rules.notes: FIXED FOR REAL (2026-08-07, Round 64, item 3) -- Round 63's 'known limitation' was correctly diagnosed for the TEXT path (pypdf's plain-text extraction really does discard all color/highlight formatting) but stopped short of checking the PDF's own underlying structure, which still carries this information. Real investigation this round, against self-built synthetic ground-truth PDFs (a real highlight, a plain negative control, and a flattened-highlight-as-colored-fill case), confirmed PyMuPDF (fitz, already a pipeline dependency via render.py) can read it directly, via TWO real methods: (1) PRIMARY -- `page.annots()` filtered for `annot.type[1] == 'Highlight'` finds a real Highlight-type PDF annotation (what Word's/Adobe's highlight tools produce, same object type PyMuPDF's own `add_highlight_annot()` creates) -- confirmed live: correctly detects the synthetic real highlight, correctly finds nothing in the negative control or the flattened-fill case. (2) FALLBACK -- some export paths flatten a highlight into a colored rectangle drawn behind the text instead of a true annotation; `page.get_drawings()` filtered to a standard highlighter color (yellow/green/pink/cyan) with real text-word overlap (via `page.get_text('words')`) catches that case too -- confirmed live: correctly detects the synthetic flattened fill, which method (1) correctly cannot see (there's genuinely no annotation object there). Either method finding anything is a fail. See pipeline/fields.py::_check_TEMP03 for the implementation and the full real investigation writeup. Needs fields['pdf_path'] (the real file), not fields['full_text']. | FIX ROUND, Section 1 Bucket D (2026-08-27): investigated the reported false positive on page 13 of a specific real document. STILL GENUINELY BLOCKED -- no fixture in this codebase reproduces it (confirmed: the existing Round 81 tests already cover and correctly EXCLUDE the one confirmed real non-highlight design element this checker's own color-range heuristic could false-positive on, cyan table/section headers -- see test_check_temp03_does_not_flag_a_cyan_fill_real_header_design_element). The checker's color-hue-range approach (yellow-through-green, or pink/magenta) is inherently a heuristic that cannot distinguish a genuine highlighter mark from ANY other colored design element (an icon, a stamp, a brand-color accent, a different-colored header style) that happens to fall in the same recognized hue family with text nearby -- without knowing what's ACTUALLY on that real page 13 (its specific fill color and shape), a fix here would be guessing at an unconfirmed pattern, the same risk this codebase has explicitly avoided elsewhere (see QA-SCH-08's own history). EXACT REAL-WORLD SCENARIO NEEDED TO UNBLOCK: the specific real document (or at minimum, a precise description of the non-highlight colored element on its page 13 -- its fill color/RGB and what it visually is) that produced this false positive, so its color/shape signature can be examined and either excluded (same as the cyan case) or used to refine the color-range boundary for real.

It is equally satisfied by the SAME tool administered twice on two different dates (an old score and a new score from one instrument) -- that is a completely normal, common re-administration pattern, not a gap. FIXED (2026-08, Round 83, item 1): confirmed real symptom -- this rule declared the whole section 'entirely blank' on a document where QA-ACF-01/QA-ACF-05's own separate reads found the date/summary fine in the same run. RECALIBRATED (2026-08, Round 82, item 3): confirmed real case -- a narrative explained that response to treatment 'could not be assessed... no direct ABA sessions were provided' due to a documented staffing gap, and this rule failed it as too generic. Investigated: the two-pole rubric above only describes 'real clinical justification for the goals chosen' vs 'vague boilerplate' -- it has NO category for a THIRD, genuinely different shape: a specific, situation-grounded explanation of why there is no clinical-progress narrative to give this period, citing a documented external cause (staffing gap, authorization lapse, family-caused cancellations, etc.). That gap in the rubric, not the original grader, was the real defect -- a narrative citing a specific, checkable, external reason is NOT the same failure mode as boilerplate that names no real detail; it just answers a different, equally legitimate question. Added third category, PASS/not_checkable (not fail): a narrative is NOT generic when it (a) states a specific, checkable reason no direct services/data exist this period (a named cause: staffing, authorization, family scheduling -- not just 'unable to assess' with nothing behind it), even if it names no clinical assessment findings, because there IS nothing to assess yet. Still FAIL a narrative that gives NO reason at all ('progress could not be determined' with nothing further) -- that remains indistinguishable from boilerplate. This does not loosen the original two-pole rubric for a document that DOES have session data to interpret -- a real progress narrative is still held to the same bar as before, and pure boilerplate on a document with real session data still fails.

See pipeline/fields.py::_check_BIP05 -- a HYBRID checker (same shape as QA-PROB-02, see that rule's own notes for the precedent): it deterministically catches ONLY this specific same-goal numeric-threshold contradiction (extracting a 'fewer than N'/'near 0'/range/bare-N occurrence ceiling from both the goal's Target Name and its own Mastery Criteria field, per goal block); when no goal states a comparable numeric threshold on both sides, or when they're stated but don't contradict, it returns not_checkable so the broader, genuinely subjective judgment call below still runs.

Original working standard (2026-07-28, still the real judgment-layer instruction for everything this DET pre-check doesn't catch): treat the criteria below as the working standard, not a confirmed-bug fix. Check the behavior target's stated Mastery Criteria (not just the goal wording) against the client's age and the behavior's own severity/safety profile: (a) for a safety-relevant behavior (elopement, aggression, self-injury), a strict zero-occurrence criterion is normal and NOT itself a fail; (b) flag only when the criterion is developmentally mismatched in a way you can point to in the text -- e.g. a criterion phrased for a skill far beyond the client's documented developmental/cognitive level, a criterion with no duration/session-count qualifier at all (just a bare percentage with no consistency window), or a criterion that ignores a stated generalization requirement (e.g. across settings/people) that the rest of the plan otherwise expects. Do not fail solely because a criterion sounds strict for a young child -- strictness alone is not the defect; an unexplained mismatch between the criterion's demand and the client's documented profile is.

rules.notes: DET if graph data is structured/tabular; needs vision LLM if graphs are embedded images. | CLARIFIED (Round 94, 2026-08-14): confirmed real disagreement across all 3 real patients this round, consistently the same direction (ma'am pass, agent uncertain/fail). This rule is already vision-eligible (VISION_ELIGIBLE_RULE_SECTIONS maps it to the 'gip_graph' page-range finder, so the relevant rendered graph image already reaches the model) -- but reading an EXACT axis date range off a rendered graph image is a much harder vision task than reading structured text, and may not be what ma'am is actually verifying in practice. Reserve uncertain/fail for when NEITHER the graph image NOR the goal's other stated dates give any basis to place the tracked period relative to the report's date range, or when a date that IS confidently readable (from either source) actually falls outside a plausible range for this auth length. | FIX ROUND, Section 1 Bucket D (2026-08-27): investigated -- confirmed this is NOT a counting/off-by-one code bug (there is no deterministic checker for this rule at all, correctly, since reading exact axis dates off a rendered graph image is a genuine vision task, not extractable structured text). No further code fix is possible here without a real improvement to the vision model's own graph-reading precision -- this is a genuine capability limit, already mitigated as far as prompt-level guidance can go, not a findable bug in this codebase's own logic.

rules.description: All goals match the POS; if goals are in the community (e.g., library), POS should reflect community
rules.notes: Concrete example added (2026-07-28 follow-up round, item 3 -- 'Quick' bucket; NOT a DET-conversion candidate -- see QA-SCH-08's own notes for why this field's real-world layout is too inconsistent for a fixed extraction pattern, confirmed against real documents in an earlier round). CORRECTED (2026-08-07, Round 63, item 8 -- confirmed real bug: this rule was passing goals that state no setting information at all, on the theory that 'no goal names a CONFLICTING setting' = compliant. That's wrong: goals saying NOTHING about setting is an inability to confirm compliance, not evidence of it, and must not default to pass.) Three distinct outcomes, not two: (1) PASS -- at least one goal's own narrative affirmatively states a setting, and every goal that states one is consistent with the declared Place of Service (e.g. POS is Office/Home/Telehealth/Community, and a goal reading 'client will complete the task across settings including office and home' names only setting(s) POS covers). (2) FAIL -- ANY goal's narrative names a setting the declared POS does NOT cover (e.g. POS is 'Office' only, but a goal reads 'client will complete the task in the community setting' or 'at home without BT present'). (3) NOT_CHECKABLE -- no goal anywhere in the document states any setting/POS information at all; this is a genuine inability to confirm the goals match the POS, not a clean pass by default. Do not collapse (3) into (1) just because there's no explicit conflict -- absence of a stated conflict is not the same as confirmed compliance. WHICH POS SOURCE, EXPLICIT (2026-08-07, Round 64, item 2 -- same fix applied to QA-GIP-09/QA-SCH-08 after a confirmed real divergence between those two rules over this exact ambiguity): read the 'declared Place of Service' above from the Hours Requesting section's stated authorized place(s) of service per CPT code, NOT the School/ABA Schedule grid's per-day POS row -- the schedule grid shows only where sessions are actually scheduled this particular week, a real, potentially narrower subset of what's authorized, and is the wrong source for this rule's own POS comparison. | UPDATED (Round 90 reconciliation, 2026-08-14): description wording changed from ma'am's checklist. Old check_type/logic kept as-is (judgment) -- verify the existing implementation still matches the new wording's intent before trusting results, especially if this was a deterministic rule. | CLARIFIED (Round 92, 2026-08-14): confirmed real double-call instability across all 3 real patients this round (Amir Howell, Arisha Haque, Solomon Schnitzer) -- when the Community Goals section is explicitly blank/N-A AND the schedule/POS table shows a single consistent non-community setting, there is nothing to conflict with: resolve to a confident PASS, not not_checkable. This is a FOURTH outcome alongside the three already listed above, not a replacement for them -- if Community Goals is blank/N-A specifically (not merely 'no goal states a setting', which is the existing outcome (3) not_checkable case), that alone is sufficient grounds for pass regardless of what the declared POS is, since there is no community goal to compare against any POS value. NOTES-ONLY fix, deliberately NOT converted to a deterministic pre-check: this rule's own notes already establish it is 'NOT a DET-conversion candidate' (see above, and QA-SCH-08's own history of 3 failed rounds of exactly this kind of regex point-fixing before being reclassified FROM deterministic TO judgment) -- inventing a new 'Community Goals:' field-label regex with zero real-document precedent anywhere in this codebase risked the same fragility. Left to the judgment layer, which can actually read the real document's own section layout. | FURTHER BROADENED (Round 93, 2026-08-14, approved): confirmed disagreement persists across all 3 real patients even with the Round 92 Community-Goals-blank carve-out -- suggesting outcome (3)'s original premise is itself too strict for ma'am's real practice, not just the one Community-Goals edge case. Proposed 5th outcome: when the declared, authorized Place of Service is a SINGLE, consistent, non-community value across every CPT code in the Hours Requesting section, and no goal's own narrative states a setting that conflicts with it, that is sufficient grounds for a confident PASS -- regardless of whether any goal explicitly restates its own setting. This reverses part of the Round 63 stance for this specific common case (a single, unambiguous, non-community POS with nothing contradicting it) while leaving outcome (3) NOT_CHECKABLE in place for the harder case Round 63 was actually protecting against: an AMBIGUOUS or MIXED declared POS (multiple different values across codes, some including community) where a goal's own silence on setting genuinely leaves the question open.

rules.description: Goals in behavioral context (SD, setting, expected response)
rules.notes: No confirmed failure example on record yet -- treat as the working standard, not a confirmed-bug fix. A passing goal's Target Goal text must contain, explicitly or unambiguously implied, all 3 elements: (1) an SD/antecedent condition -- what cues or triggers the behavior (e.g. 'when told no', 'when a demand is given', 'when BT is distracted'); (2) a setting/context if the goal is context-dependent (e.g. 'in a conversation', 'during a task'); (3) an expected response stated as an observable action, not a vague internal state (e.g. 'will mand by calling BT's name' is fine; 'will feel less anxious' is not, because there's no observable response). Fail when the antecedent condition is entirely missing (the goal reads as a bare behavior with no stated trigger) or when the expected response is an internal/emotional state with no observable action attached -- not merely because the goal is short.

rules.description: Mastery criteria age/ASD-appropriate; no 0%, use 'fewer than one instance'
rules.notes:
Converted from judgment to deterministic (2026-07-28 round, item 1 backlog): the zero/near-zero-endpoint ban is a per-goal pattern check over an extractable field (Mastery Criteria), same shape as GIP-10 -- see pipeline/fields.py::_check_GIP16, which shares GIP-10's _goal_block_starts helper. Scope note: this DET check covers ONLY the zero-value-ban half of the rule's description ('no 0%, use fewer than one instance'); the broader 'age/ASD-appropriate' framing in the description is not separately implemented here since no distinct check for it was ever built or described beyond the zero-ban itself -- if a genuinely separate age-appropriateness judgment is intended beyond the zero-ban, that would need its own rule/check. This ban applies to BOTH percentage-based AND frequency-based mastery criteria - do not treat frequency/count goals as exempt just because they don't use a percent sign. A mastery criterion is a violation if it states a zero or near-zero endpoint in ANY of these forms: '0%', '0 occurrences', '0x', 'near 0 levels', 'near 0', or equivalent zero-value phrasing - regardless of Sampling Method (Percent Correct or Frequency). Any of these must instead read 'fewer than one instance' (or an equivalent minimum-occurrence phrasing). Verified live: Reeda has exactly 2 confirmed violations (page 26 Tantrum, page 27 Elopement, both in 'Target Name:' Behavior Reduction Goal blocks -- not 'Target Goal:' ones, which is why the shared block-splitter covers both marker forms). Charny has zero violations (one goal reads '0-2 occurrences over three consecutive days', correctly NOT flagged since it's a range, not a zero endpoint). EXPLICIT DIVISION OF LABOR WITH QA-GIP-10 (2026-08-07, Round 63, item 7): a BLANK Mastery Criteria is a real problem, but this rule's own zero/near-zero pattern never matches an empty string, so on its own this would silently pass a blank field -- QA-GIP-10 already flags a blank Mastery Criteria, but ONLY for a goal block that also has a Sampling Method field (it skips any block without one). This rule now flags the one remaining gap -- a blank Mastery Criteria in a block with NO Sampling Method field either -- and deliberately does NOT also flag the Sampling-Method-present case, to avoid two rules reporting the same blank-field violation as if it were two separate problems. If both this rule and QA-GIP-10 pass on the same document, that means every Mastery Criteria field found is confirmed non-blank; a not_checkable from either is not itself evidence of a blank field.

BROADENED (2026-08, Round 83, item 2a): confirmed real miss -- '0 times a week' is the same absolute-zero problem as '0%', just phrased with 'times' instead, and the prior pattern didn't recognize it. _ZERO_MASTERY_PATTERN now also catches '0/zero times', '0/zero occurrences', '0/zero instances', and a bare '0'/'zero'/'none' as the field's entire value. Still deliberately does NOT match 'fewer than N'/'less than N' for any N -- that phrasing is this rule's own recommended non-zero rewording, not a violation. | FIX ROUND (2026-08-26): added 'current level' alongside 'mastery criteria' to scope, per ma'am's ask. check_type left as deterministic (_check_GIP16 already exists and is registered) but its CODE was not changed in this pass to actually also inspect current-level fields -- confirmed not reached this round. Flagged, not silently assumed done. | FIX ROUND, Section 1 (2026-08-27): REAL GAP FOUND AND FIXED -- the 2026-08-26 round added 'current level' to this rule's own description but flagged, in its own notes, that _check_GIP16's code was not changed to match ('confirmed not reached this round'). Now fixed: _check_GIP16 also checks each goal block's own 'Current Data:' field (the real field name for a goal's current-level value, confirmed on the real sample TP) against the SAME zero/near-zero pattern already banned for Mastery Criteria -- but deliberately does NOT apply the blank-field failure to Current Data (a blank current-level reading commonly just means no data collected yet for a newly-started goal, a different, legitimate situation from a blank Mastery Criteria, which is a real setup problem regardless of goal age). | Fix Round (2026-09-10), item 25 -- REVERSAL, CONFIRMED WITH MA'AM DIRECTLY: she is now asking for this rule to check ONLY the Mastery Criteria field, not current data or any other field -- reversing the 2026-08-26/2026-08-27 change above. Description and _check_GIP16 both reverted to Mastery-Criteria-only. Flagged explicitly, not silently treated as a bug fix: this walks back a real, deliberate earlier request of hers.

rules.description: Goals observable/measurable with SD, deficit, expectation
rules.notes: Same family as GIP-11 -- same caution: no confirmed failure example on record yet, working standard only. A passing goal must contain: (1) an SD/antecedent condition (what prompts the target); (2) a deficit statement -- what the client currently cannot do or does incorrectly, stated concretely enough that progress against it is measurable; (3) an expectation stated as an observable, countable action (percent correct, count, duration -- not a vague internal-state description). Fail when the goal is observable/measurable in form (has a Mastery Criteria percentage) but the Target Goal text itself never states what deficit is being remediated, or when the antecedent condition is missing entirely -- a goal can have a perfectly quantitative Mastery Criteria and still fail this rule if the goal statement itself doesn't establish what's being measured and why.

rules.description: 3+ parent training goals/auth period, no 'caregiver' wording (or rationale if used)
rules.notes:
Three independent criteria, all must hold -- confirmed via real evidence on multiple documents that a compressed one-line description let these slip past unnoticed:
(1) At least 3 distinct parent-training goals exist for THIS authorization period. Count only goals under 'Goals in Progress' / currently active for this auth period -- do NOT count goals listed under 'Mastered Goals' toward this total, even if they use parent-training wording, since those are from a prior period. (Confirmed failure mode: a document with 4 'Mastered Goals' phrased as parent-training goals but only 1 actually current/in-progress goal -- the '3+' requirement is about the current period, and miscounting mastered history toward it produces a false pass.)
(2) No individual CURRENT goal's own Target Goal text uses 'caregiver' as its subject (e.g. 'The caregiver will...') instead of 'parent'/'parents'/'mother'/'father', unless that specific goal has its own accompanying rationale for the wording choice. IMPORTANT: this document type routinely uses 'Parent/Caregiver' as standard SECTION-HEADER and narrative terminology (e.g. 'Parent/Caregiver Involvement:', 'Parent/Caregiver Goals:', 'caregivers are coached on...') -- that widespread usage is NOT itself a violation of THIS sub-criterion and must not be read as making 'caregiver' wording normal everywhere in the document. This specific check is narrower: does any individual CURRENT goal's own subject specifically say 'caregiver' while its sibling current goals say 'parent(s)'/'mother'/'father'? That specific inconsistency, without a rationale for that one goal, is a fail under this sub-criterion.
(3) FIXED (2026-08-08, Round 78, item 1 -- closes the cross-section gap flagged as a known limitation in Round 63; real miss confirmed on Yisroel Leibowitz's real TP, where foster care is noted under Biopsychosocial Information but the Parent/Caregiver section's own generic header-level 'Parent/Caregiver' language carries no rationale anywhere in the document). Read the WHOLE document, not just this section, for any indication that the child's caregiver is NOT a biological/legal parent -- foster care, kinship care, a non-parent guardian, a grandparent raising the child, a group-home placement, or any other stated non-parent caregiving arrangement, wherever it appears (commonly Biopsychosocial Information or Educational History, but check anywhere). Do not key this off the single literal phrase 'foster care' -- recognize the underlying fact pattern (someone other than the child's parent is the caregiver) however it's actually phrased. If such an indication IS present anywhere in the document: a rationale for using 'Parent/Caregiver' / generic 'caregiver' language (instead of naming the specific relationship, e.g. 'foster parent' or 'grandparent/guardian') must appear SOMEWHERE reasonably tied to that language -- in the Parent/Caregiver section itself, or elsewhere explaining the choice. Its absence is a fail under this sub-criterion, even if criteria (1) and (2) both pass and even if the document's 'Parent/Caregiver' phrasing is only ever used at the section-header/narrative level (which sub-criterion (2) above treats as normal in the ordinary case -- this sub-criterion is the deliberate exception for when a real non-parent-caregiver fact is on record elsewhere). If NO such indication is found anywhere in the document, this sub-criterion is satisfied by default (nothing to justify) -- do not fail a document with no stated non-parent-caregiver fact just because it uses 'Parent/Caregiver' as ordinary header language.
COUNTING SCOPE (confirmed second false-pass mechanism, on a document where the mastered-goals exclusion above was already applied correctly): only count entries listed literally under a 'Parent/Caregiver Goals:' (or equivalent parent-training goal list) heading for the current period. A 'Transition Plan' / hours-titration section that discusses parent training being 'mastered and maintained' in its narrative, or that lists the PATIENT's own skill-mastery criteria in a numbered table (e.g. 'When [patient] can make 5 relevant comments...'), is not a parent-training goal and must not be counted toward the 3+ total just because it sits near parent-training language or references future parent-training phases. If, after excluding both Mastered Goals and any non-goal-list narrative/tables, fewer than 3 distinct current parent-training goals remain, this is a fail regardless of how much surrounding text discusses parent involvement generally.

CLARIFIED (2026-08, Round 85, item 2): confirmed real miss on Blythe Diaz's TP -- the required 3 Program Goals correctly use 'Parent,' but the document also has additional SUPPLEMENTAL parent-training-adjacent goals beyond those 3 that happen to use 'Caregiver' wording; the ground-truth reviewer's own standard is a clean Pass here, since those extra goals are beyond the required minimum and their wording doesn't affect it. Sub-criterion (2) above, read literally, never said this -- it just said 'No individual CURRENT goal's own Target Goal text uses caregiver,' with no distinction between the (up to) 3 goals actually being counted toward the minimum and any supplemental goals beyond it. That ambiguity is corrected here: sub-criterion (2)'s caregiver-wording check applies ONLY to the goals actually being counted toward the 3+ minimum (the same set counted for sub-criterion (1)) -- a supplemental goal beyond that minimum using 'Caregiver' wording, with no rationale, does NOT violate sub-criterion (2) and does not affect the pass. If choosing which (up to) 3 goals count is itself ambiguous (e.g. more than 3 parent-training goals exist and it's unclear which are 'the required 3'), prefer the reading that credits the document -- a genuine, unambiguous violation still requires an identifiable specific goal using unrationaled 'caregiver' wording among the goals needed to reach the minimum, not merely SOME goal somewhere in the document doing so.

rules.description: COC includes provider name/title/date; session note detailed
